title: RebuttalOutput
description: Bounded cross-examination output. Both sides use this exact schema; only the `side` value differs. One round only.

side.description: Must match the side you were assigned. Submitting the other side is rejected.

responses.description: One entry per opposing claim you are responding to. May be empty. Responding to fewer claims honestly is better than responding thinly to all of them.

targetClaimId.description: A claim ID from `opposingVerifiedClaims`, written exactly as supplied including its side prefix (e.g. DRIVER-C1). Targeting your own claim, or an ID that is not in the context, is rejected.

stance.description: CHALLENGE means the claim is incomplete, misleading, or does not support the conclusion drawn from it — never that the verified measurement is untrue.

reasoningSummary.description: A concise statement of your position. Not a place to think out loud; internal deliberation must not be included.

evidenceIds.description: Evidence IDs from the supplied context only. There is no new evidence in this round; never invent an ID.

policyRuleIds.description: Policy rule IDs from the supplied context only. Never invent a rule.

assertedFacts.description: Measured values quoted from the trusted context, so they can be verified. A value that contradicts the trusted analysis is rejected.

concessions.description: Target claim IDs you are conceding. Every entry must correspond to a response whose stance is CONCEDE or PARTIALLY_CONCEDE. Listing a claim you challenged is rejected.

overallSummary.description: One to three sentences summarising your response to the opposing case.
